summary: The change records a stop's kind once, at checkError's seventeen sites, and carries it through the result, the marker and the skill to the resume line, with no wording reads left in resumeLine. The version gets a patch bump and every touched file has its Docs entry. Three findings share a cause: the facts that decide what a resumed shaper is told hold in the cases the loop test measures, but not in three others. Those are a revise-only pass over an earlier run's folder, a result check that runs before the spec check, and an adjustment to a decided task. The fourth finding is two comments that still describe the old wording reads. No scheduled or queued work touches these paths.

findings.title: A resumed first shape in a revise-only pass can rewrite over an earlier run's decided entries
findings.description: The PR keeps the from-scratch sentence for a resumed `shape r<n>` (workflows/redline-loop.js:708-709) because no decision can be on disk at that point. It states this as measured fact in resumeLine's comment (682-685), in docs/running.md, "Run markers and resume" ("At a round's first shape ... nothing you or the autopilot decided can be in the folder yet"), and in the replay standard (agent-os/standards/workflow/replay.md:19). That is true within one launch, which is what the spec measured over the loop test's scenarios. It is not true for `/redline:redline-revise <pr> round N`. skills/redline-revise/SKILL.md:9 and :15 take the newest `*-<pr>-review-round-<N>` folder as `revise.specFolder`, and that folder can be one an earlier run wrote. workflows/redline-loop.js:5280 shapes in that folder under the label `shape r<N>` (3851-3852). Suppose the earlier run shaped and resolved round N with a decision. Then the folder's shape.md holds entries ending `Decided by: @<login>` or `Decided by: redline (autopilot)`, and plan.md holds their tasks. If this pass stops at a shape-stage check and is resumed, it is told to "Rewrite plan.md, shape.md, standards.md and references.md in the spec folder from scratch, replacing what the earlier attempt wrote", over those entries. This needs four things: the debug entry point, run over a round an earlier full run had already resolved with a decision, a stop at the shape stage, and a resume. The rewrite at a resumed first shape is also the base branch's behaviour. What is new in this PR is the claim that such a rewrite cannot meet a decision. The earlier run's record commit keeps those entries in git history.
findings.proposedFix: Limit the claim to a round folder this launch created, in the comment at 682-685, in docs/running.md and in the replay standard. Or give a revise-only pass's `shape r<n>` the reshape's restore clause when its folder already held shape.md at launch. At minimum, correct the docs sentence.

findings.title: The restore clause tells a resumed reshape to keep a decided task that an adjustment may move
findings.description: A reshape resumed after a stop with no ownCheck gets the clause at workflows/redline-loop.js:712. It says to "keep any entry the person or the autopilot decided and the task written for it" and "Never rewrite". That clause is appended to the reshape prompt, which says "Apply each adjustment" (2223) and asks for each decided finding's files "as plan.md holds it when you are done" (2209). docs/running.md, "A reshape after your decision", also says a reshape can move a decided finding's task and that "the run follows the plan as reshaped (#106)". So when the approver's adjustment is to a decided finding's task, the resumed prompt gives two instructions that disagree about that task, and the clause makes no exception for an adjustment. agents/redline-shaper.md rule 9 says the same ("keep every decided entry and its task"). Neither the ownCheck clause (711) nor the base branch's hold clause says to keep a task: both say to read the tasks as left and correct what the error names. The case needs a decided round, a bounce whose adjustment names a decided finding's task, and a reshape that stopped with no ownCheck (a call that returned nothing, or the spec check) and was then resumed. If the rerun keeps the task, the next approve bounces the same adjustment. With maxPlanAdjustments at its default of 2 (line 111), a resumed `reshape r<n> #2` that keeps the task ends the run at stage approve (4245-4252). A resumed `#1` costs one more cycle, because `#2` carries no resume line. The loop test scripts every agent, so it cannot show which instruction a live shaper follows.
findings.proposedFix: Write "keep any entry the person or the autopilot decided, and the task written for it unless an adjustment above changes that task" in the clause at 712, and the same in agents/redline-shaper.md rule 9. Pin the phrase in tests/loop-test.mjs.

findings.title: A result check that runs before the spec check marks a refused-Write stop as Redline's own
findings.description: vetShape runs four checks before `await checkSpec(...)` at 3825: the disposition check (3818-3821), checkDispositions (3822), checkSecondLook, and checkCalls (3824). The PR makes these throw checkError with ownCheck true. checkSpec's missing-file stop deliberately carries no field, because "a file can be missing because a Write was refused, which a person does fix" (spec shape.md decision 14; docs/running.md). Suppose one shaper attempt leaves plan.md or shape.md unwritten and also returns a result that fails one of the earlier checks (a finding left out, or an ask with no call). The first check throws, checkSpec never runs, and the catch returns ownCheck true (5471-5476). The skill then says nothing needs fixing by hand and offers to resume as it stands (skills/redline/SKILL.md:272). A resumed reshape gets the correct-what-the-error-names clause (711), which does not mention the missing file, instead of the restore clause (712). Under the same permission mode the rerun meets the refused Write again. At best it then stops at the spec check with ownCheck false, one relaunch later. This needs a refused or halted Write (#76; PR #54 round 2) in the same attempt as a result that fails a check. PR #54 round 2's halted shaper returned every finding with its own calls, so that incident alone would not hit this. The resolve's checks also carry ownCheck, and no folder check follows the resolve. So a resolve whose Writes were refused and whose result fails a check is marked the same way, although nothing reads the folder at the resolve either before or after this PR. The check order is the base branch's; the field it now sets is this PR's.
findings.proposedFix: Run checkSpec before the ownCheck checks in vetShape. Or, when a result check throws, still run the spec check and let its failure win, with ownCheck false. Pin it with a loop-test scenario whose shaper leaves out a finding and writes no shape.md, and expect ownCheck false.

findings.title: Comments still say the resume line reads an error's words, and that a resumed reshape rewrites
findings.description: Three comments describe the old behaviour. The hold's comment at workflows/redline-loop.js:4289-4290 says "Both messages open with the same words, which the resume line reads (resumeLine)", but resumeLine now reads the entry's ownCheck (705-712) and never the error's words. The comment at 4295-4296 says the resume line tells the rerun "to correct the task the error names", but the clause now says "correct what the error names". checkSpec's header at 3398-3399 says a spec-check stop "names the shaper, so a resume reruns it with the replace sentence", but a resumed reshape now gets the restore clause (712) and only a first shape gets the replace sentence. These comment blocks sit outside the diff's hunks. The change that made them stale is inside the diff.
findings.proposedFix: Rewrite 4289-4290 to say the hold raises through checkError (ownCheck) and resumeLine reads the field. Change 4295-4296 to "correct what the error names". Rewrite 3398-3399 to say a resumed first shape gets the replace sentence and a resumed reshape gets the restore clause.

accounting.ref: Claim: a marker from before 0.4.5 is refused at startup because the skill passes ownCheck null. Evidence against: skills/redline/SKILL.md:52 tells the skill to pass false when the marker holds no ownCheck, and the workflow takes false (workflows/redline-loop.js:288-291), so the entry resumes as an ordinary stop. Nothing in the path reads the missing key with jq. Null reaches the check only if the skill ignores that sentence.

list.summary: A stop whose real cause is a refused Write can be reported as Redline's own check, so the skill says nothing needs fixing by hand. In vetShape, three checks that set ownCheck (the missing-disposition check at 3818, checkDispositions and checkCalls) throw before `await checkSpec(...)` at 3825. The spec left ownCheck off the spec check on purpose, because a missing file can be a refused Write the person must fix (#76, PR #54 round 2). But when one attempt both leaves no plan.md or shape.md and returns a short or inconsistent JSON, the result check fires first and the stop carries ownCheck true. The resolve's eight checks have the same blind spot, with no folder check after them at all. Fix: run checkSpec before the checks that set ownCheck. No first-run prompt changes, because spec status already follows every shape. Alternatively, when a result check fails, still run the spec check and let its failure win with ownCheck false. Pin it with a scenario that drops a finding and a spec file together.
list.failure_scenario: A self-hosted run under --plugin-dir in auto mode, where subagent Writes are refused (#76). `reshape r1 #1` cannot write shape.md and its JSON leaves out R1-2. The error is 'the shaper gave no disposition for R1-2' with ownCheck true. The skill says nothing needs fixing by hand and offers to resume as it stands, so the person resumes without changing the permission mode. The reshape is told to read the four files 'as that attempt left them' and correct what the error names (shape.md is missing), instead of the restore clause. Its Write is refused again and it stops again.

list.summary: Pre-existing: the new claim that no decision can be on disk when a first shape is resumed does not hold for `/redline:redline-revise <pr> round N`. That path reuses an existing round folder (`revise.specFolder`, the newest `*-<pr>-review-round-N`). The redline-revise skill says this can be a folder an earlier run wrote. If that run shaped and resolved the round, the folder holds `Decided by: @<login>` entries, and a resumed `shape rN` is still told to rewrite the four files from scratch over them. The from-scratch behaviour is unchanged by this PR, but resumeLine's comment, docs/running.md ('nothing you or the autopilot decided can be in the folder yet') and the replay standard now state the opposite as measured fact. Fix: limit the claim to a round folder this run created, or give a revise-only pass over a folder that already holds shape.md the restore clause. At minimum, correct the docs sentence.
list.failure_scenario: Round 2 of an earlier full run was shaped, resolved and record-committed, so its shape.md holds the person's decided entries. Someone runs `/redline:redline-revise 120 round 2`. `shape r2` stops at a result check and is resumed. Its line says 'Rewrite plan.md, shape.md, standards.md and references.md ... from scratch, replacing what the earlier attempt wrote' in a folder that holds decided entries, which the docs say cannot happen.

list.summary: The new restore clause for a reshape resumed after a crash or the spec check tells it to 'keep any entry the person or the autopilot decided and the task written for it', and 'Never rewrite'. That can be read as leaving a decided finding's task as it is, against #106: a reshape exists to apply the approver's adjustments, which may move or change a decided task ('the run follows the plan as reshaped'). The ownCheck clause and the old hold clause both said to correct what the error names, with no ban on editing tasks. agents/redline-shaper.md rule 9 has the same wording ('keep every decided entry and its task'). Fix: say to keep each decided entry and its task as the earlier attempt left it, unless an adjustment in the prompt changes that task, and change rule 9 to match.
list.failure_scenario: A decided round where the plan approver bounces with an adjustment to the task of R1-1, a fix the person decided (move it from app/x.php to app/y.php). `reshape r1 #1` returns nothing (API error) before applying it. On resume the restore clause says to keep R1-1's task, so the rerun can leave it on app/x.php. The approver bounces the same adjustment again, and each crash or spec-check resume repeats this until maxPlanAdjustments stops the run at approve.

list.summary: A resume from a marker written before 0.4.5 can be refused at startup instead of resuming as an ordinary stop, as decision 18 promises. The validation `entry.ownCheck !== undefined && typeof entry.ownCheck !== 'boolean'` refuses `null`. `run read` and `run check` print an older marker as stored, with no ownCheck key, so the skill has to invent `false`, and a jq-style read of the missing key gives `null`. `fail()` throws before the workflow's try block, so there is no result and no marker update. Fix: treat `null` as absent in the check, or have `run read` and `run check` (scripts/redline-prefs.sh) fill in `ownCheck: false` for a marker without it. Add a prefs-test case for a marker that has no ownCheck.
list.failure_scenario: A run stopped under 0.4.4 at `recheck r1`, and the plugin was updated to 0.4.5. The skill builds the entry from `marker.ownCheck`, which is missing, and passes `"ownCheck": null`. The workflow throws 'args.resume must map an agent label to {attempt, error, hand, ownCheck}' before any agent runs, and every retry from that marker fails the same way.

list.summary: Two comments still describe the old behaviour. The hold's comment at 4289-4290 says 'Both messages open with the same words, which the resume line reads (resumeLine)', but resumeLine now reads ownCheck, and the point of this change is that it never reads an error's words. checkSpec's header at 3398-3399 says a spec-check stop means 'a resume reruns it with the replace sentence', but a reshape resumed after the spec check now gets the restore clause, and only a first shape gets the replace sentence. Fix: rewrite both comments to say the hold raises through checkError (ownCheck), and that a resumed reshape gets the restore clause.
list.failure_scenario: A maintainer trusts the hold's comment, rewords its message, and adds a startsWith test back into resumeLine. Or a maintainer believes the checkSpec comment and expects a resumed reshape to rewrite from scratch, which is exactly what #117 removed.
